title: Back-to-School Eye Exams for Pine Beach Kids | Academy Vision
metaDescription: A school screening is a helpful start, not a full eye exam. Book your child’s exam before classes start at Academy Vision in Pine Beach, NJ.
h1: Start the School Year with a Complete Eye Exam in Pine Beach
kicker: Ready for the New School Year?
lede: New teachers, new classrooms, more reading—and eyes that have to keep up with all of it. A complete eye exam before classes begin shows how your child is really seeing, so you start the year with answers instead of guesses. At Academy Vision in Pine Beach, we keep kids’ exams gentle, simple and tailored to their age.

sections.heading: What a School Screening Can Miss
sections.html:
School vision screenings are quick, helpful checks. Many ask a child to read letters or shapes from across the room, which can catch trouble seeing at a distance.

A screening isn’t an eye exam, though. It often doesn’t test how well the eyes focus up close, how they team up, or whether they’re healthy, so a child can pass and still struggle with reading, homework or screens. Our article on pediatric eye exams beyond school screenings goes into more detail.

sections.heading: Why Back-to-School Timing Works
sections.html:
• Good timing. Back-to-school season is a practical time to book, especially if your child hasn’t had a recent comprehensive exam, has a changing prescription, or has shown signs of a vision problem.
  • A comfortable visit. We take a gentle approach that helps kids feel at ease from the moment they arrive.
  • Clear answers for you. We talk through what we find in plain language, so you know whether anything needs attention before the first day.

sections.heading: What Your Child’s Exam Checks
sections.html:
During the exam, we:

  • Test how sharply your child sees at different distances, from the board to a book.
  • Evaluate how their eyes focus and work together for reading and close work.
  • Look at overall eye health and development.
  • Keep everything age-appropriate and easy to follow.

sections.heading: A Familiar Place for Local Families
sections.html: For over 40 years, families in and around Pine Beach have trusted us with their vision, and many return year after year from Pine Beach, Beachwood and Toms River. If your child needs glasses, we offer lightweight, durable children’s frames suited to school, play and everyday wear. Take a look at our kids’ eyewear.

sections.heading: A Screening Once vs. an Exam Every Year
sections.html: A screening is a snapshot of one day. Children’s eyes keep changing as they grow, and a prescription that worked last fall may not be right this fall. The American Optometric Association recommends annual comprehensive eye exams for school-age children, or more often when their eye doctor advises it. Yearly visits let us compare results over time, and if nearsightedness is creeping up, we can talk with you about myopia management.

sections.heading: More Care for Growing Eyes
sections.html: A back-to-school exam is one part of our children’s eye care, which spans first exams, glasses and help with a prescription that keeps changing. You can also learn more about our pediatric eye exams.

faq.q: My child passed the school screening. Do they still need an exam?
faq.a: A pass is good news, but it only covers what the screening tested. A comprehensive exam also looks at focusing, eye teamwork and eye health, which a screening usually doesn’t measure.

faq.q: What signs should I watch for?
faq.a: Squinting, frequent eye rubbing, headaches after reading, covering one eye, losing their place on a page, or sitting very close to screens can all be reasons to book. Kids often don’t mention blurry vision, because they assume everyone sees the way they do.

faq.q: Can we book siblings at the same time?
faq.a: If it’s easier to schedule your children together, we can do that. Just mention it when you call (732) 978-9306.

faq.q: Is late summer the only good time to book?
faq.a: Back-to-school season is a convenient time, but there’s no need to wait for it. If you notice signs of a vision problem during the school year, that’s a good reason to come in sooner.

cta.heading: Book Before the First Bell
cta.html: Give us a call at (732) 978-9306 or book online to schedule your child’s eye exam before school starts.
